text:
Happy Tuesday! Monday's clouds have cleared out, and we're sitting in full sunshine after a chilly start. It's still on the cool side this morning, but the sun does the work from here. We climb to around 53 this afternoon, with the European model a touch cooler, so call it low 50s and you'll be about right. The breeze is light, so a jacket is plenty for a lunch walk, and the best stretch for getting outside is early afternoon, since the sun sets at 4:23.

Clouds build in tonight, and the low settles around 39, a bit milder than this morning. Wednesday is partly sunny and warmer, with a high near 56. Everyone agrees on that number.

The dry, mild stretch keeps going toward 60 by Friday. Showers don't show up until late Sunday.

Any precipitation will be very light and should remain fairly localized; it will gradually taper off by early afternoon. No other changes were needed.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: A potent ridge and associated area of surface high pressure will become established this week, making it feel as if it were still mid-October. In a classic El Nino pattern, deep troughing and strong surface lows over the Pacific have caused continuous southwest to westerly flow out west, flooding the Great Plains and western Canada with warm Pacific air. This has caused temperature anomalies in the 20-30+ degree range. This airmass will begin to arrive today aloft, but clouds will likely remain stuck under the inversion, so it will likely take until Tuesday to warm up. Some undercast is likely today due to a shrinking and lowering moisture layer. Starting Tuesday, highs in the 50s will prevail though 60 will be possible in some of the warmest areas. There will be a strong, persistent subsidence inversion, and it will aided by the fact that significantly more surface heat will be lost at night than will be able to be replenished by the sun during the day. Radiational cooling will help lows drop into the 20s and 30s, around climatological normals.Temperatures at summit level should reach well into the 40s and freezing levels look to eclipse 10,000 ft by late in the week. KEY MESSAGE 2: Surface high pressure will be centered south of our region Thursday night into Friday, then drift northward across our area Saturday before sliding east. This will provide the northern New York and Vermont area with mainly dry weather and temperatures warmer than seasonal normals. On Sunday a low pressure system north of the Great Lakes will track northeastward, and our region will be under southerly flow ahead of the cold front. Sunday could be the warmest of the period, but will see increasing clouds and chances for showers on Sunday as well. We may have a cold front cross the area Sunday and bring some scattered rain showers. But there is also a possibility with two low pressure centers that the better energy associated with each low will pass to our north and to our south, leaving us in between without a lot of precipitation. Still much to work out before we get to the end of next weekend, but at this time this may be our best chance for showers through the period.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Tuesday! For the most part, any clouds from Monday have now cleared, which means we started the day cooler with most places in the 20s and lower 30s. Clear skies and sunshine will continue through the day, warming us back up into the upper 40s and low to mid 50s by this afternoon. Tonight will be a bit warmer, with overnight lows settling into the mid to upper 30s by early Wednesday morning. Through Wednesday there may be a few more clouds mixing in from time to time, but with that being said, still plenty of sunshine as temperatures climb toward the mid and upper 50s, with some spots approaching 60. It’s a very similar story for Thursday with partly cloudy skies overhead, and temperatures again in the mid and upper 50s if not close to 60. Friday looks like it will be the warmest day of the week, as mostly sunny skies overhead will help drive our temperatures toward the upper 50s and low to mid 60s, possibly for some spots to the south. We head into the weekend on a nice note for Saturday with mostly sunny skies overhead and temperatures again heading toward the upper 50s and low to mid 60s. Just a degree or so cooler than Friday. Sunday again looks a degree or two cooler than Saturday. We start Sunday dry, but we could find the chance of a few showers by later Sunday evening and night. A few showers may linger into early Monday, but we are dry by later in the day. Temperatures are cooler Monday, back in the 40s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-16T23:55:00Z — same caveat): Brighter and milder Tuesday — Tuesday marks the transition toward brighter and warmer weather. Expect a partly to mostly sunny sky, with highs reaching the low to mid-50s. The Wednesday through Friday stretch looks beautiful, with plenty of sunshine and highs in the upper 50s to low 60s! The nice stretch continues this weekend, as it stays mostly dry and mild. Expect nearly full sunshine Saturday. A south breeze picks up on Sunday, as a cold front approaches. A few late-day showers are likely. Highs will be near 60 both days. Behind the front, more seasonable air returns early Thanksgiving week. Highs fall back to the 30s and low 40s. A few showers are possible around the holiday, as it turns a bit milder.
